title: Debugging and Testing
description: Learn techniques and tools to identify and fix errors in your JavaScript code, and how to write tests to ensure code quality.

lessons.title: Introduction to Debugging
lessons.content: Debugging is the process of finding and fixing errors or bugs in your code. It helps you understand why your code isn't working as expected and how to correct it.

lessons.title: Using console.log() Effectively
lessons.content: The simplest way to debug JavaScript is using `console.log()`. It prints values and program flow in the console, helping you trace variable states and function calls.

lessons.title: Basic Debugging with Browser DevTools
lessons.content: Modern browsers offer developer tools with features like breakpoints, stepping through code, inspecting variables, and watching expressions. These help debug complex problems interactively.

lessons.title: Breakpoints and Step Execution
lessons.content: Breakpoints pause program execution at specific lines, allowing you to examine the state of variables and the call stack before continuing or stepping through the code.

lessons.title: Common JavaScript Errors
lessons.content: Common errors include syntax errors, reference errors, type errors, and logical errors. Recognizing these helps you pinpoint where things go wrong.

lessons.title: Example: Using console.log() for Debugging
Introduction to Testing
lessons.content: Testing involves writing code that verifies your program behaves as expected. Tests can catch bugs early and ensure your code stays reliable as it grows.

lessons.title: Types of Tests: Unit and Integration
lessons.content: Unit tests focus on individual functions or components, while integration tests verify that multiple parts work together correctly.

lessons.title: Writing a Simple Unit Test (Conceptual)
Best Practices for Debugging and Testing
lessons.content: Use debugging tools regularly, write tests for critical code, keep tests small and focused, and automate tests to run frequently during development.
